name: Junior software developer annual wage (BLS software-developer occupation, 25th percentile as junior proxy)
tier_note: Junior tier: entry/junior engineers (BLS has no experience split; P25 proxy + platform cross-checks)
why_it_matters: Base price of a junior hire; sets the economics of junior hiring and whether the junior pipeline still pays for itself.
threshold_note: Junior P25 crossed USD 100K in the 2023 survey (101,200).

name: Median software developer annual wage (US national, occupation-wide)
tier_note: All-experience tier (context curve; control for the May-2022 OEWS methodology break)
why_it_matters: Anchors the ladder; headline BLS series for the occupation.
threshold_note: Median crossed USD 120K in the 2021 survey (120,730).

name: Senior software developer annual wage (BLS 75th percentile as senior proxy)
tier_note: Senior tier: senior engineers (P75 proxy + Levels.fyi cross-checks)
why_it_matters: Marginal cost of senior capacity; sets the arbitrage between AI leverage and human senior judgment.
threshold_note: Senior P75 crossed USD 150K in the 2021 survey (151,960).

name: Staff/principal software developer annual wage (BLS 90th percentile as staff+ proxy)
why_it_matters: Top-of-ladder pay tracks whether top-of-market (big-tech) comp is spreading to the broad market.
threshold_note: P90 crossed USD 200K in the 2023 survey (208,620); note the May-2022 BLS methodology break inflates the 2022 jump.

name: Seniority premium proxy (P75 wage / P25 wage, within-year BLS table)
why_it_matters: Stable = structural premium; compression = ladder flattening; widening = experience scarcity.
threshold_note: Band 1.64-1.67 across the whole window; no crossings.

name: Junior-level total comp at big-tech firms (Google L3 / Meta E3 single-firm proxy)
tier_note: Big-tech tier (single-firm proxy: Google L3, Meta E3)
why_it_matters: Tells whether the entry ladder into top-of-market jobs widened or stayed flat over the window.
threshold_note: Google L3 ~USD 189K (2019) to ~USD 188K (2023): flat in nominal terms.

name: Top-paying company median total comp for entry-level engineers (rank-1 by year)
tier_note: Top-of-market entry tier (levels.fyi rank-1: Lyft/Two Sigma/Jane Street/HRT)
why_it_matters: Extremes of dispersion at the top of the entry ladder versus the flat big-tech median.
threshold_note: Rank-1 crossed USD 300K in 2023 (Jane Street 325K) and USD 400K in 2024 (HRT 410K).

name: Junior engineer market-median total comp (levels.fyi by-level table)
tier_note: Junior tier, total-comp basis (2 public years; context view)
why_it_matters: Direct market-median view of junior total comp cross-checking the BLS P25 wage series.

name: Senior engineer market-median total comp (levels.fyi)
tier_note: Senior tier, total-comp basis (2 public years; context view)
why_it_matters: Direct market-median view of senior total comp cross-checking the BLS P75 series.

name: Hourly wage 10th percentile, BLS software-developer occupation (junior proxy, hourly basis)
tier_note: Junior tier, hourly basis (robustness view on the annual P25 series)
why_it_matters: Same story as the annual P25 ladder but from published hourly percentile columns.

name: Hourly wage median, BLS software-developer occupation
why_it_matters: Hourly-basis context curve.

name: Hourly wage 90th percentile, BLS software-developer occupation (staff+ proxy, hourly basis)
why_it_matters: Hourly-basis mirror of the annual P90 series.

name: Entry-level Software Engineer base pay, Payscale panel (self-reported)
tier_note: Junior tier, self-reported panel (page-average basis in most years; 10yr window)
why_it_matters: Weak but long-window junior panel; noisy; do not headline.

name: Senior Software Engineer base pay, Payscale panel (self-reported)
why_it_matters: Weak but long-window senior panel.

name: Senior/junior base-pay page-average ratio, Payscale panel
tier_note: Derived from Payscale panels (level-titled junior vs senior)
why_it_matters: Independent junior-vs-senior premium view at level-titled extremes.
threshold_note: Rising 1.41 (2016) to 1.57 (2025): level-titled seniority premium widened on the self-report panel.

name: Average starting salary, CS bachelor graduates (NACE salary survey)
why_it_matters: Direct new-grad starting-salary view complementing the BLS P25 proxy.

name: Median listed wage, H-1B labor condition applications for job title "Software Engineer"
tier_note: Mediated junior tier (H-1B certified petitions wage floor)
why_it_matters: Wage floor for visa-mediated hiring; tracks junior wage under DOL/USCIS review.
threshold_note: Sept 2025 proclamation collapsed consular H-1B receipts >90% short-term (DHS technical appendix).

name: Median listed wage, H-1B labor condition applications for "Senior Software Engineer"
why_it_matters: Wage floor for senior visa hiring.

name: CS bachelor degrees conferred, US (NCES digest of education statistics)
why_it_matters: If supply keeps growing while entry demand shrinks, junior wage compression follows.

name: Software development job-postings index, Indeed Hiring Lab (Jan 2020 = 100)
why_it_matters: Falling postings = collapsing demand; sets candidates wage-negotiation power.

name: Unemployment rate, US computer/mathematical occupations (BLS CPS LNU04034021)
why_it_matters: Low unemployment = upward wage pressure; a rise = slack.
threshold_note: Never spiked above ~4% in the window; ~3.3% in 2025.

name: Professional developers currently using AI tools (Stack Overflow survey)
tier_note: Adoption proxy for AI capability at work
why_it_matters: AI leverage is the potential junior-vs-senior constraint; adoption up = possible compression of junior premium.

name: All developers using or planning to use AI tools (Stack Overflow survey)
why_it_matters: Same as above, broader basis.
bound_source: unit definition: share of developers, bounded 0-100 percent (not a physical limit)

name: Daily AI use (SO 2025) + Copilot subscriber/user official datapoints
why_it_matters: Confirms conversion from experimentation to daily habit.

name: Credential gate for entry-tier engineering (degree/CS requirement vs skills-based hiring and apprenticeships)
why_it_matters: The gate that turns training pipelines into juniors; opening it multiplies supply into a shrinking entry tier.
qualitative_justification: Bootcamps collapsed 2023-25 (Turing School closed Apr 2025; BloomTech CFPB order), Andela abandoned junior-first Sep 2019, degree requirements eased 2021-24, federal skills-based hiring push June 2025; Multiverse exited US.
threshold_note: Two for-profit entry-pipeline builders failed inside the window while the nonprofit variant persists.

name: AI capability as a drop-in substitute for junior engineering output
why_it_matters: Directly competes with the whole point of hiring juniors; sets the threshold inverting the junior pipeline.
qualitative_justification: SWE-bench class agents ~14% (2024) to ~78% (2026) per cited sources; Anthropic May 2026 claims >80% of its own code Claude-authored; Stanford Canaries show adjustment via hiring not wages.
threshold_note: Drop-in positioning tried by Devin (2024) and repriced ~25x lower; product survives as leverage, not replacement.

name: Geographic arbitrage on SWE pay (global remote talent vs US seniority bands)
why_it_matters: Alternative to US juniors/seniors; regulates the wage floor of the whole ladder.
qualitative_justification: COVID remote normalization (2020) fell; RTO rigidity and location-based pay bands re-tightened 2023-25; EOR compliance commoditized (Deel et al).
threshold_note: Andela pivot to seniors (Sep 2019); arbitrage now concentrated at senior+ rates.

name: Information asymmetry in SWE pay (who knows what the band is)
why_it_matters: Transparency compresses negotiation spreads, mostly at the edges of the ladder.
qualitative_justification: CO 2021, NYC Nov 2022, CA Jan 2023, EU PTD deadline Jun 7 2026 (partially met), first EU reports Jun 2027.
threshold_note: US posting-range regime is now standard for tech employers; EU phase begins 2026-27.
